central_claim: Increasing inference compute improves accuracy up to a task-dependent saturation point, beyond which extra compute adds cost and latency without reliable accuracy gain.

mechanism.text: This is the most important non-results cell -- an architecturally blocked combination, not merely unstudied.

beats.heading: Beam search requires scoreable intermediate steps.
beats.text: In Snell et al., a PRM scores each solution step, top candidates are kept, branches extend from them. The method presupposes reasoning serialized into inspectable chunks.

beats.heading: BDH-CQ's intermediate states are not decoded.
beats.text: Intermediate reasoning states are "not decoded into language" (BDH-CQ technical report, Section 1). There are no step boundaries to branch at, and no published per-step verifier that could score a partial latent state H_r.

beats.heading: Diversity is harder than it looks.
beats.text: Geiping et al. Section 7 demonstrate path independence: re-initializing from multiple starting states s_0, "the model moves in similar trajectories... The same orbital patterns, fixed points, or directional drifts emerge regardless of initialization." So the obvious way to generate candidate diversity in latent space -- resampling the initial state -- converges to the same behavior anyway.

mechanism.closing: Nobody has published this. It is an open question. Here is what would need solving first.
mechanism.source: BDH-CQ technical report Sec. 1; Geiping et al. 2025 Sec. 7.

bdh_cq__beam_search.hard_rule: No chart, no axis, no dotted 'hypothetical' line for this cell. Text, equations, and a structural diagram showing where a verifier would have to attach -- nothing that could be read as a result.

mechanism.text: Force a minimum amount of reasoning: when the model tries to stop and give its answer, suppress that stop and append "Wait" to make it keep reasoning, up to a fixed number of forced continuations, before taking its final answer.

quotes.text: we suppress the generation of the end-of-thinking token delimiter and optionally append the string "Wait" to the model's current reasoning trace to encourage the model to reflect on its current generation

mechanism.note: s1-32B was fine-tuned on 1,000 curated reasoning traces (s1K) with an explicit end-of-thinking delimiter. Our own model (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct) has no such trained delimiter, so we approximate the same mechanism structurally: we suppress the model's natural stop and inject "Wait, let me double check that." to force continuation. This is our own implementation of the technique, not a reproduction of s1-32B's numbers.
mechanism.source: Muennighoff, Yang, Shi, Li, Fei-Fei, Hajishirzi, Zettlemoyer, Candes, Hashimoto (2025). s1: Simple test-time scaling. arXiv:2501.19393, Section 3.1.

results.note: Our own sweep, forced continuations in {0,1,2,4}, GSM8K, per-problem results.

slider.description: Reveals per-problem prediction vs. gold answer, and whether forcing the model to keep reasoning changed its answer.

mechanism.text: Budget forcing intervenes on the decoded token stream -- suppressing a stop, injecting "Wait" text. Huginn generates tokens autoregressively like any LM, so the technique is compatible in principle. But Huginn already has its own, different test-time compute dial: the r recurrence depth, which spends compute before any token is decoded, not by manipulating text already on the page. We did not run this combination -- unstudied by us.
Architecturally blocked, for the same root reason as beam search.

beats.heading: Budget forcing needs a decoded thinking trace to intervene on.
beats.text: The technique works by suppressing an end-of-thinking token delimiter in the generated text and appending "Wait" to that text (Muennighoff et al. Sec. 3.1). It presupposes reasoning that exists as tokens on the page.

beats.heading: BDH-CQ's reasoning states are not decoded.
beats.text: The H_r reasoning recurrence produces latent states that are, per BDH-CQ Section 1, "not decoded into language" until the final H_R is passed to G_theta. There is no intermediate token stream to suppress a stop in, and nowhere to inject "Wait."

beats.heading: The same wall as beam search.
beats.text: This is architecturally the identical limitation that blocks BDH-CQ x Beam search: both methods require a decoded, inspectable intermediate trace, and BDH-CQ's reasoning loop never produces one.

mechanism.closing: A second cell blocked by the same root cause -- not a coincidence, but a direct consequence of reasoning in undecoded latent space.
mechanism.source: BDH-CQ technical report Sec. 1; Muennighoff et al. 2025 Sec. 3.1.

bdh_cq__budget_forcing.hard_rule: No chart, no axis, no dotted 'hypothetical' line for this cell.

mechanism.text: Dual recurrence: a memory recurrence that accumulates as demonstrations are ingested, and a reasoning recurrence layered on top. Unlike Huginn's r, effort here is not a free continuous dial -- the model is trained with different levels of latent reasoning exposure, and at inference you choose among those trained levels (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH), not an arbitrary iteration count.

results.also_cite: 150M-parameter model, 29.5% pass@2 on ARC-AGI-1 public eval, $0.00070 computed cost per task. Independently audited (Section 5, 'Independent evaluation').
results.label: Published result -- BDH-CQ technical report, Table 5. BDH-CQ's checkpoint is not public; we did not reproduce this.
results.hard_rule: Never plot Huginn and BDH-CQ numbers on the same chart. Different models, different tasks (GSM8K vs ARC-AGI-1), different metrics (exact match vs pass@2). Show as two separate panels sharing a conceptual label only.

latent_compute.text: BDH itself has no depth dial. Its state recurs over tokens, indexed by token t, with layers L fixed at training time (Kosowski et al. 2025, Eq. 8). BDH-CQ added a separate reasoning recurrence H_r on top. That addition is BDH-CQ's contribution, not something inherited from BDH.

best_of_n.text: BDH scales inference the way a transformer does -- by consuming more tokens. But its state rho is fixed-size regardless of sequence length. Kosowski et al. describe it as "associative memory (like KV-cache, but organized differently)" and state "there is no notion of a context window" (Section 4.1). So token-scaling does not grow BDH's memory the way it grows a transformer's KV-cache.

beam_search.text: BDH scales inference the way a transformer does -- by consuming more tokens. But its state rho is fixed-size regardless of sequence length. Kosowski et al. describe it as "associative memory (like KV-cache, but organized differently)" and state "there is no notion of a context window" (Section 4.1). So token-scaling does not grow BDH's memory the way it grows a transformer's KV-cache.

budget_forcing.text: BDH scales inference the way a transformer does -- by consuming more tokens. But its state rho is fixed-size regardless of sequence length. Kosowski et al. describe it as "associative memory (like KV-cache, but organized differently)" and state "there is no notion of a context window" (Section 4.1). Budget forcing also presupposes a decoded reasoning trace it can intervene on -- BDH-CQ's H_r loop never produces one (see the BDH-CQ x Budget forcing panel).

do_not_claim: BDH is a module appended to a transformer (it is a complete standalone architecture).
Swapping in BDH reduces inference cost at equal accuracy (no such result is published).

failure_moment_1.title: Saturation, task-dependent (Huginn)
failure_moment_1.description: Switch task type in the Huginn x Latent-compute panel above and watch the slider: OpenBookQA and GSM8K saturate at different points, using our own real per-problem sweep data. The paper's own Table 1 shows the same pattern in their numbers -- OpenBookQA accuracy at r=4, 8, 16, 32: 28.2% -> 35.4% -> 37.6% -> 38.8%. Look at the gaps: +7.2pp, then +2.2pp, then +1.2pp -- each doubling of compute buys a smaller gain. GSM8K CoT, by contrast, goes from 0.00% at r=1 to 34.80% at r=32 in their data -- still climbing hard over the same range where OpenBookQA had already flattened. Same dial, same model, two different tasks, two different saturation points.
failure_moment_1.misconception_corrected: More thinking time always makes an AI smarter.

failure_moment_2.title: The statistical null (published, BDH-CQ Section 6.6)
failure_moment_2.authors_quote: All four reported endpoints favor STANDARD in point estimate, but this comparison is statistically unresolved.
failure_moment_2.lesson: Not merely that returns diminish, but that sometimes you cannot statistically distinguish whether the extra compute helped at all.
